predictions.selection_reason: property assignment -> directly sets object property -> may assign attacker-controlled value leading to prototype pollution or property injection
predictions.source_summary: The 'value' and 'key' come from iterating over properties of 'obj' using forOwn, which iterates over own properties. The 'obj' comes from the 'objects' argument passed to the defaults function, which can be any user-provided object.
predictions.sink_summary: The assignment 'o[key] = value' directly modifies the target object 'o'. If 'key' is '__proto__' or similar prototype-polluting keys, this could modify the Object prototype.
predictions.guard_summary: The assignment only occurs if 'o[key] == null' (line 20). The isObject check (line 22) only applies to nested objects, not the top-level assignment. No validation or sanitization of keys is present. The forOwn library only iterates own properties, but does not prevent prototype-polluting keys.
predictions.risk_pattern: Direct assignment of user-controlled keys to target object without prototype pollution protection, allowing modification of object prototype if keys like '__proto__' are provided.
predictions.context_summary: The defaults function recursively merges properties from source objects into a target object. The candidate statement assigns values to the target object when the property doesn't exist (is null/undefined).
unresolved_facts: Exact behavior of 'for-own' dependency regarding prototype properties
Exact behavior of 'is-plain-object' dependency regarding prototype checks

top_sast_rules.cwe_name: Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Prototype Attributes ('Prototype Pollution')
